readout_other: mechanical withdrawal threshold (von Frey); heat withdrawal latency (Hargreaves plantar test); spinal IL-6 and IL-10 (ELISA); spinal Iba1 immunohistochemistry
direction_notes: Therapeutic ultrasound (alone or combined with treadmill training) increased mechanical withdrawal threshold and heat withdrawal latency (reduced allodynia/hyperalgesia) after chronic constriction injury, and suppressed spinal IL-6 and Iba1 upregulation while increasing IL-10; the TU+TT combination gave the largest effect.

exposures.label: Pulsed 1 MHz therapeutic ultrasound over the sciatic nerve CCI site, alone (group 5) or combined with treadmill training (groups 3, 6)

target.label: skin over the sciatic nerve surgical (CCI) incision

timing.protocol_description: Under light isoflurane (1%) anaesthesia, an S-size probe was applied with gel using a gentle circular movement over the skin incision, 5 minutes/day, 5 days/week for 4 weeks beginning postoperative day 3 (groups 3 and 6 had TU followed by 30 minutes of treadmill training; group 5 had TU alone).

source_quotes.n_subjects: Methods. Each group contained 10 rats. Group 1 underwent only the CCI procedure. Group 2 underwent a sham operation where the sciatic nerve was exposed but not ligated. Group 3 had the sham operation followed by both TT and TU. Groups 4, 5, and 6 underwent the CCI procedure followed by TT alone, TU alone, and both the TT and TU interventions, respectively. Heat and mechanical sensitivity, interleukin-6 (IL-6), interleukin-10 (IL-10), and ionized calcium binding adaptor molecule 1 (Iba1) were evaluated.
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: After the animals were lightly anesthetized with isoflurane (1%), a TU device (US-750, Bunkyo-ku, Tokyo, Japan) was used while the transducer was applied to the skin of rats with gel. The parameters were 1 MHz with pulse (20% duty cycle), 1-W/cm<sup>2</sup> intensity, and 100-Hz frequency (beam nonuniformity ratio3.6) for 5 minutes a day. To prevent damage by cavitation, the S-size ultrasound probe was used in pulsed mode and applied with a gentle circular movement applied over the skin incision.

flags.reason: paper states 10 rats per group for the three groups receiving ultrasound (sham-TT-TU, TU-alone, CCI-TT-TU) but never a combined total; recorded as a list of group sizes.

paper states duty cycle (20%) and PRF (100 Hz) but never a separate pulse-duration figure; dividing duty cycle by PRF would give the pulse duration but this is arithmetic the paper does not state, so left not_reported.
paper states '1-W/cm2 intensity' without naming the domain (free-field vs at-skin) or the intensity metric (ISPPA vs ISPTA/ISATA); placed under isppa_w_cm2 by default.

the study includes a surgical sham (sciatic nerve exposed but not ligated) as a control for the CCI injury, but the authors explicitly note in their Limitations that no ultrasound-device-off (inactive transducer) control arm was included in this experiment.
paper gives only the device model (US-750) and a city (Bunkyo-ku, Tokyo, Japan), not a named manufacturer.
